label: input s at the start of the sequence (t=0, or t=1 after a/w/d/c/f/s)
explanation: Token-and-position feature for the letter s at the very start of the original sequence. When the first original token (t=0) is s it fires every time at a constant maximum (1.463); this case carries 96% of the activation mass. It also fires, much more weakly (about 0.1-0.4 of max), when s is the second token (t=1) and the first token is one of a, w, d, c, f, s. Within that group it is strongest after s/a and weakest after f. It never fires on s at t>=2, on any other token, on the delimiter, or anywhere in the copy phase. The simpler predicate (t==0 & in_tok==s) gets dev precision 1.0, recall 0.83, mass recall 0.96.

issues: None found. On the test split the predicate scores precision 1.0, recall 1.0, F1 1.0 and mass recall 1.0, and misses --split test shows 0 missed activations and 0 false positives.

The dev profile backs every claim: activation mass is 100% in the original phase and 0 in the delimiter and copy phases; t=0 carries 0.960 of the mass and t=1 carries 0.040, with nothing at t>=2. The only input token that fires is s, the median activation equals the max of 1.463, and at t=1 the feature fires only after prev_tok s/a/w/d/c/f. Mass shares there are s 0.009, a 0.009, w 0.008, d 0.006, c 0.005, f 0.003, so it is highest after s or a and lowest after f, as claimed.
The simpler predicate t==0 & in_tok==s scores on test: precision 1.0, recall 0.83, mass recall 0.96, which matches the claim.
Minor wording point: 'constant maximum at t=0' is supported (median = max = 1.463), but this was not checked step by step.
